newsitem.title: GERMANY: German industry welcomes Krupp-Thyssen talks.
newsitem.headline: German industry welcomes Krupp-Thyssen talks.

text.p: The Federation of German Industry (BDI) on Thursday welcomed talks set to begin later in the day aimed at merging the steel activities of Krupp and Thyssen, two of Germany's biggest and most well-known industry groups.

The two companies agreed on Wednesday to begin talks on Thursday and hoped to reach agreement within eight days, an unexpected development after Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp's surprise hostile takeover bid on Monday for its larger rival Thyssen AG.
BDI president Hans-Olaf Henkel told German radio that the a merger of the steel activities of the two companies could have broader implications for German industry.

"This will lead to a greater competitiveness of the German steel industry," said Henkel, adding that the concentration of the steel industry in other countries such as France and Britain led to considerable cost advantages.

Henkel said he did not expect the two companies to have any problems gaining approval from cartel authorities for a merger of their steel companies Thyssen Stahl AG and Krupp Hoesch Stahl AG, based in Duisburg and Dortmund in the Ruhr Valley.

The new company would have a share of around 15-20 percent of the European steel market which means the European Commission, not Berlin, would rule on the merger. The new company would not have a dominant market position in Europe.

Henkel also dismissed the "partially hysterical" attacks on Krupp from the German press and some politicians about its hostile takeover bid for Thyssen, a rare move in Germany that sparked fierce criticism of Krupp and its banks.
"Mergers are normal," said Henkel. "We have to get used to takeovers; they could make sense."
